page: Amazon Web Services r5n.8xlarge is a memory-optimized, network-optimized, and EBS-optimized server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. This configuration delivers 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache, alongside support for AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets.

The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage, relying instead on EBS optimization for storage needs. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that single-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng, geekbench, and single-threaded compression tasks. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. The instance achieves an average of 25.79 million operations per second for Redis SET operations and 20.75 GB/sec for static web serving. LLM inference speeds are average for small and medium models but poor for large 70B models. This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and network-bound applications that benefit from high memory capacity and 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth rather than high single-core compute performance.
